procedure.description: suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema

denial.carcText: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer.
denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 15877 (suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema) with date of service 2026-02-24. CARC 56: Procedure/treatment is deemed experimental/investigational by the payer. Payer remark: Coverage criteria in the medical policy for lipedema were not met based on the documentation submitted.

criteria.text: Diagnosis of lipedema stage II or III documented on examination: bilateral symmetric disproportionate adiposity of the limbs sparing the feet, negative Stemmer sign, tenderness, and easy bruising.
At least 6 months of conservative therapy including compression garments and manual lymphatic drainage or supervised exercise, with persistent pain or functional impairment.
Pain or impaired mobility attributable to lipedema.

chart.text: Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 4 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

38 year old woman here about her legs, self-referred after reading about lipedema. Mother and aunt had the same legs. Discussed lymph-sparing liposuction, staged, and that it is debulking, not a cure. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Surgeries: no prior surgery. Allergies: no drug allergies. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Classic picture. Column legs out of all proportion to her waist, cuff sign at the ankles, feet spared, Stemmer negative, exquisitely tender to pinch over the thighs, bruises if you look at her. Stage 2. She has been in class 2 flat-knit compression daily for 13 months, MLD weekly with the lymphedema therapist across town, water aerobics twice a week, and she is still in pain and the legs have not budged. Says she cannot stand through a shift anymore, pain in the thighs is constant, stairs are hard because the legs knock together.
Lymphedema therapy visit. Manual lymphatic drainage both lower extremities, compression check, garments fitting well, she reports wearing them daily. Pain unchanged at 6 out of 10.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports no real change.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports slight improvement that does not last.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Session 5. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Follow-up. Reviewed photos and measurements, legs unchanged. Went over the staged plan and the compression afterward. Vitals today 118 over 68, pulse 64.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 199, LDL 153, HDL 40, triglycerides 166. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Blood pressure check. 143 over 72 today, 125 over 75 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Pre-op for stage one, thighs. Consent signed. Marked standing. Garments ordered.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 56 denial can be answered from the record.
